claims.nodeLabel: Defense Support Program (DSP) missile early warning satellites
claims.sourceText: GAO-03-825R, Military Space Operations, 2 June 2003, govinfo, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/GAOREPORTS-GAO-03-825R/html/GAOREPORTS-GAO-03-825R.htm
claims.text: GAO's description of the system and its dates: DSP is 'a strategic surveillance and warning satellite system with an infrared capability to detect ballistic missile launches', the programme commenced in 1967, the first operational satellite was deployed in 1971, the most recent launch was August 2001, and it 'provides near real-time detection information in support of DOD's integrated tactical warning and attack assessment (ITW/AA) mission'.

claims.text: Replacement history: 'The SBIRS-High program is focused on replacing DSP', after the earlier Advanced Warning System, Follow-On Early Warning System and Alert, Locate, and Report Missiles programmes were abandoned as too expensive or technologically immature.

edges.note: The thesis's cited Osedacz database is drawn from ballistic missile early warning satellites in geosynchronous orbit, which is what DSP is; the thesis does not name DSP and no opened government document names it either, so the identification is attributed and not asserted.
